Paged read looks sound; inspect backup logic for data-loss/integrity defects.
The middle of backup.ts, where the backup is written, was cut off; read it to check how records are paged and counted.
See the rest of verifyBackup and restore to check whether the trailer's record count and header counts are validated against the body.
Read the elided part of backup creation (collection enumeration and per-collection reads) to check whether every record gets into the backup.
Backup/paged-read look careful; inspect collections handling (find/count/limits) for a defect.
Look at how collections apply pending writes, ordering and limits within a mutation for correctness defects.
Look at how mutations merge pending writes with paged reads; find/count over pending writes is a likely spot for a correctness defect.
Read the base collection operations (find/count/limit handling) for read-path defects.
Inspect the mutation-side find/count/query overlay logic for correctness defects (limits, ordering, counts).
Read the base collections class (find/count/query) that was truncated, to check paging and limit handling.
Read CollectionReader's find/query/count to compare unpaged vs overlaid behavior.
Inspect the transaction's query overlay and the write and commit paths for defects.
Inspect update/delete pending-write logic for version/overlay bugs within a mutation.
Collections and backup code look sound so far. Next I'm checking session expiry and token comparison in identity for defects that can be proven.

Inspect the capability call timeout/abort handling for leaks or success-on-failure.

The capability ledger leaves a record in 'sending' at line 196 and ignores the updateIfVersion result at line 208. Before writing a test I need to see how the ledger and the invoker are built.

A mutation's view filters its own pending writes with matchesWhere (collections.ts 98-109), where compare(undefined, x) is -1, so a record missing the field matches `lt`/`lte`. I need FeltDB's own range semantics for missing fields to see whether committed reads disagree.
